entries.name: HUD_QueueMessage
entries.evidence_/_notes: Nitrodon's annotated stunt disassembly shows this long-call target receiving message IDs for Wipeout (`0x0E`), Head Bounce (`0x10`), Tabletop (`0x11`), flip/roll/twist/Z-flip result messages, and praise messages. Exact queue/render split still needs local call-graph validation.

entries.name: Stunt_FinalizeAndScoreAirTricks
entries.evidence_/_notes: Nitrodon's focused `stunts.txt` plus bank-82 listing expose the complete landing/finalization pipeline: roll/flip quarter-turn accumulation, half-twist conversion, Z-flip/tabletop handling, wipeout/headbounce checks, trick-message selection, stunt-combination indexing, praise lookup, and reset of transient stunt state.

entries.name: Player_ApplyVerticalAcceleration
entries.evidence_/_notes: Nitrodon's bank-82 annotation is directly supported by the instruction flow: current-player Y velocity is capped below `0x0200`, upward motion receives +19, downward acceleration is `19 - Yvel/32`, the result is added to Y velocity, and current-player Y coordinate is incremented.

entries.name: Input_DecodePlayer1Buttons
entries.evidence_/_notes: Nitrodon's bank-82 listing shows raw controller words `$030D/$030F` decoded into explicit A/X/L/R/B/Y/select/start flags and normalized vertical/horizontal direction fields at `$0311/$0315`.

entries.name: RNC1_Unpack
entries.evidence_/_notes: Identified by unique opcode-structure match to preserved 1992 SNES `RNC_1.S`; ROM offset `0x00B8F1`. Regional/build equivalents: Europe retail `01:B8E2` (`0x00B8E2`), 1994-11-29 PAL prototype `01:B8D1` (`0x00B8D1`), legacy beta identical to USA.

entries.name: RNC1_MakeHuffTail
entries.evidence_/_notes: Preserved Method-1 MAKEHUFF tail begins here; final RTS at `01:BB6E`, establishing the shipped generic RNC1 body end.

entries.name: RNC1_ReadWordLoROMSafe
entries.evidence_/_notes: Integration helper used by the shipped Method-1 decoder for a 16-bit packed-stream read through `IN`. Normal path returns `LDA [IN]` while restoring the pointer; when `IN=$FFFF`, it fetches the high byte from next-bank `$8000`, matching LoROM linear-stream continuity across a bank boundary. `01:BB73` is the helper's wrap-test `BNE`, not a store.

entries.name: APU_UploadBlockById_Wrapper
entries.evidence_/_notes: Exact bytes `JSR $8082; RTL`. Callers load X with audio block IDs before entering; the body at `02:8082` performs the SPC handshake and calls `APU_ResolveBlockPointer` at `02:812A`, establishing X as a block-record selector.

entries.name: APU_ResolveBlockPointer
entries.evidence_/_notes: Exact static routine maps block ID X onto the packed audio-record pool beginning at `10:8000`. It walks X length-prefixed records, performing LoROM bank-wrap arithmetic, and returns the selected record pointer in DP `$63-$65`. Package-table IDs `$00-$31` address the first 50 records, but direct setup calls pass IDs through at least `$42`; the same contiguous parser resolves records `$32-$42`. Therefore `$00-$31` is the package-table ID universe, not the resolver's upper bound.

entries.name: Text_HandleFCPositionControl
entries.evidence_/_notes: Bounded static analysis of the Sayans translation-control grammar. The routine preserves A, recognizes low-byte `FC`, consumes the following parameter, scans subsequent character bytes until `FF` or `FB`, consults `Text_TestCharacterMetadataBit7` for ordinary bytes, then computes `parameter * 32 + horizontal adjustment` into DP `$9F`. The 32-column arithmetic and translated `FF FC xx` / `FB FC xx` sequences support a centered tilemap-position/layout role. Exact user-facing meaning of the parameter remains unpromoted.

entries.name: Text_TestCharacterMetadataBit7
entries.evidence_/_notes: Shared helper reached from four text/layout loops including `03:8998`, `00:C4CB`, and `00:C510`. It indexes the byte table at `00:C6F8` by character code and tests bit 7. Printable-table inspection shows uppercase A-Z in the low half while lowercase a-z, digits and much punctuation usually carry bit 7; therefore this is a verified character-metadata class test, not yet a proven glyph-width flag.

entries.name: Frontend_CurrentMenu
entries.notes: Verified in both native and Snes9x/snesref deterministic runs: `0xD7` main menu, `0x3C` one-player rider select, `0x6D` first one-player tours page, `0xF6` one-player track select, `0x16` now-playing screen, then `0x00` after race entry.

entries.name: Frontend_SelectedOption
entries.notes: Recovered bot uses it for main-menu/tour selection. Native captures show `0x00` at clean main menu and first tours page, consistent with bot policy.

entries.name: Frontend_SelectedRow
entries.notes: Recovered bot label; native route captures row `0x00` through the verified clean frontend route. Exact semantics outside these menus not yet tested.

entries.name: Frontend_SelectedColumn
entries.notes: Recovered bot label; native captures change with frontend scene/selection. Rider-select ready state captures `0x06`, matching the bot's left-column target value.

entries.name: Race_ActiveState
entries.notes: Recovered bot label `inRace`; verified as `0x01` after deterministic race entry in both native and Snes9x/snesref runs. Non-race screens can contain other transient values, so only `0x01 = active race` is currently asserted.

entries.name: Course_ActiveDecodedPayload
entries.notes: Confirmed by run 36514985916: active Dragster decoded stream 1 matches 33,814/33,815 bytes from this address; only decoded byte 11 is runtime-mutated.

entries.name: Player1_XPosition
entries.notes: Effective recovered-bot word key `xPos`. Race-acceleration run 36512546762 moves it identically in native/reference from 1088 at rest to 1655 under staged Right input, alongside positive X speed.

entries.name: Player1_YPosition
entries.notes: Effective recovered-bot word key `yPos`. Sustained-B run 36514981164 causally changes player 1 from ground Y=859 in the matched no-B control to Y=797 while airborne; native and Snes9x match exactly.

entries.name: Player1_XSpeed
entries.notes: Effective recovered-bot word key `xSpeed`; bot explicitly sign-converts it. Race-acceleration run 36512546762 changes it identically from 0 to +447 under Right input while X position increases.

entries.name: Player1_YSpeed
entries.notes: Effective recovered-bot word key `ySpeed`; bot sign-converts it. In run 36514981164 sustained B changes it causally from 0 in the matched control to -21 while player 1 is airborne; native and Snes9x match exactly.

entries.name: Player1_AirTime
entries.notes: Dynamic run 36514981164 causally changes the low byte from 0 to 9 under sustained B while Y position/speed enter the airborne trajectory. Nitrodon's WRAM map identifies the slot as time in air with a 9-frame maximum, and bank-82 stunt code reads it as a word (`LDA $0545,Y`). Historical bots read only the low byte.

entries.name: Player1_PitchAngle
entries.notes: Persistent player-1 pitch/orientation. From control angle `0x07`, eight L frames produce `0x37` (= 7−16 mod 64) and eight R frames produce `0x17` (= 7+16 mod 64), identically native/reference. ROM `02:8D84` copies working `$0F49` into this slot.

entries.name: Player2_PitchAngle
entries.notes: Paired player-2 pitch/orientation slot. Sibling ROM routine at `02:9272` executes `LDY $0F49; STY $04C9`; surrounding destinations shift coherently to player-2 fields.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_PitchScratch
entries.notes: Historical bot reads this as `pitch`, but static sibling routines copy the same working value into persistent player-1 `$04C7` or player-2 `$04C9` slots. L-vs-control checkpoints leave `$0F49` unchanged while `$04C7` changes causally, so it should not be treated as stable player-1 storage.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_HalfTwistCount
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies this as the current-player number of half-twists. The stunt finalizer at `02:9C2E` shifts it right once to derive full twists, caps the result at 4, and feeds that into the stunt-combination index. Writer analysis independently shows current-player copy/clear/increment behavior.

entries.name: Player1_TabletopDuration
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map and annotated bank-82 code identify this as tabletop duration; `INC $042F,X` at `02:9582` advances it and `02:9C87` requires duration >= 3 to emit the Tabletop message. Dynamic run 36776825024 independently observes X input driving low-byte `0→1→2→3→4→0` at a two-frame cadence in native and pinned Snes9x. This supersedes the older accumulated-count label.

entries.name: Player1_ZFlipCount
entries.width: 16-bit slot; low byte used by USJO
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies the player-specific slot as Z-flip count. Bank-82 code reads/writes it under 16-bit accumulator mode, caps the landing result at 4, and uses it directly in the stunt-combination index. USJO v8 reads only the low byte.

entries.name: Player1_RollCount
entries.width: 16-bit slot; low byte used by USJO
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map explicitly records a 2-byte player-1 roll count. The stunt routine increments it with 16-bit `INC $11F9,X` after four quarter-turn progress steps, and may credit a 3/4 roll on landing. USJO v8 reads only the low byte.

entries.name: Player1_FlipCount
entries.width: 16-bit slot; low byte used by USJO
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map explicitly records a 2-byte player-1 flip count. The stunt routine increments it with 16-bit `INC $11FD,X` after four quarter-turn progress steps, and may credit a 3/4 flip on landing. USJO v8 reads only the low byte.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_BoostMeterWorking
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map distinguishes this shared current-player boost meter from stable player slots at `$11CF/$11D1`. Bank-82 code zeroes it on wipeout, subtracts 16 in an off-screen penalty path, clamps computed boost to `0x0180`, and feeds half the value into velocity limiting. USJO v8 reads only its low byte as a zero/nonzero gate.

entries.name: Player1_ZRotationState
entries.width: 16-bit slot; low byte used by USJO
entries.notes: Static scan run 36769525945 exposes paired copy structure: `02:8AB2` loads `$0DFD` and stores it to shared working `$0F57`, while `02:8FBA` loads paired `$0DFF` into the same working slot and `02:8DB2` copies `$0F57` back to `$0DFD`. This strongly supports `$0DFD/$0DFF` as paired persistent racer Z-state slots; exact physical interpretation remains open.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_ZRotationWorking
entries.width: 16-bit working slot; low byte used by USJO
entries.notes: Static scan run 36769525945 shows `$0F57` as shared current-player working state: `02:8AB2` copies player-1 `$0DFD` into it, `02:8FBA` copies paired `$0DFF` into it, `02:8DB2` writes it back to `$0DFD`, and later bank-02 code mutates/clears it. USJO v8 calls the low byte `zprerotation`; exact physical semantics remain open.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_XVelocityWorking
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies current-player X velocity here. Bank-81 collision/transform code reads `$0F9F/$0FA1`, transforms both through matrix terms, and stores the new X/Y pair back; bank-82 movement and boost paths also mutate `$0F9F`. This resolves USJO's old “alternative speed” comment as shared current-player working state rather than a second player-1 field.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_YVelocityWorking
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map and bank-81 velocity transform pair this with `$0F9F`; bank-82 vertical-acceleration code at `02:A968` updates this slot directly.

entries.name: CurrentPlayer_Index
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map records `0 = player 1`, `2 = player 2`. Bank-82 stunt/movement code repeatedly loads it into X/Y to index paired 16-bit player slots.

entries.name: Player1_BoostMeter
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies the stable player-1 boost slot, distinct from shared current-player working `$11CD`. Local copy-in/copy-out path should still be named explicitly.

entries.name: Player2_BoostMeter
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies the paired player-2 boost slot.

entries.name: Player1_RollQuarterProgress
entries.notes: Bank-82 stunt code increments this progress value and converts it into one roll when it reaches 4, then resets it; paired player-2 slot is `$1203`.

entries.name: Player1_FlipQuarterProgress
entries.notes: Bank-82 stunt code increments this progress value and converts it into one flip when it reaches 4, then resets it; paired player-2 slot is `$1207`.

entries.name: Player1_FacingAtTakeoff
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map says this records whether the racer was facing right when leaving the ground. The stunt finalizer uses it to decide whether accumulated quarter-turn direction maps to flip versus roll; paired player-2 slot is `$033D`.

entries.name: Player1_NextCheckpoint
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies the next-checkpoint field; paired player-2 slot is `$119B`. High-value race-finish fixture target.

entries.name: Player1_FinishGateState
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map records `0` when player 1 can cross the finish line; paired player-2 slot is `$119F`. Exact nonzero state meanings remain open.

entries.name: Player1_LapsRemaining
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies laps remaining; paired player-2 slot is `$0EF3`.

entries.name: Stunt_CurrentScore
entries.notes: Nitrodon's map identifies the current score on stunt tracks. Score update semantics remain to be traced.

entries.name: Player1_StuntAirLatch
entries.notes: Olivier retained this as an “Air flag”; Nitrodon's stunt disassembly shows `02:9A97` setting indexed `$1361` to 1 during stunt-air initialization and `02:9D88` clearing it during finalization. Exact relationship to ordinary air-time `$0545` remains open.

entries.name: Camera_ScreenXPosition
entries.notes: Historical TAS watch list labels this “Screen X Position.” Not consumed by v8; local camera/unit semantics still need validation.

entries.name: Player1_FacedDirection
entries.notes: Recovered bot: 1 = right, 0 = left. Not yet independently validated.

entries.name: Player1_ArrowsVisible
entries.notes: Effective duplicate-key address used by recovered bot; 0 means direction arrows showing.

entries.name: Player1_ArrowDirection
entries.notes: Effective duplicate-key address used by recovered bot; 0 = right, 1 = left.

entries.name: Race_CountdownTimer
entries.notes: Recovered bot word key shared by players. In run 36512546762 it decreases identically in native/reference by exactly `0x0100` per guest frame across the staged pre-start/acceleration checkpoints. Exact game-facing units/threshold meanings remain to be named.

entries.name: Race_ReverseControls
entries.notes: Recovered bot: 2 = controls reversed, 0 = normal. Not yet independently validated.
